skills.title: What Plants Need to Live
skills.description: Plants need air, water, light, heat, nutrients, and space. Can you pick what a plant needs and what could harm it, like drought or frost?

skills.title: Parts of a Plant
skills.description: Plants have roots, stems, leaves, flowers, stamens, pistils, seeds, cones, and fruit. Can you label each part and match it to its job?

skills.title: Plant Life Cycles
skills.description: Plants change as they grow, from seed to sprout to adult plant that makes new seeds. Can you put the stages in order?

skills.title: How Plants Adapt and React
skills.description: Plants change to fit where they live, like leaves turning toward light or cactus storing water. Can you match each plant to how it reacts?

skills.title: Plants Make Their Own Energy
skills.description: Plants use sunlight to make energy. They take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. Can you pick what goes in and what comes out?

skills.title: People Use Plants
skills.description: People around the world use plants for food, shelter, medicine, and clothing. Can you match each plant use to the right group?

skills.title: Plants We Eat and Where
skills.description: We eat roots, stems, leaves, fruits, and seeds, including plants grown by First Nations, Métis, and Inuit. Can you match food plants to where they grow?

skills.title: Plants and Animals Need Each Other
skills.description: Plants give animals and people food and oxygen, and animals help plants with pollen and seeds. Can you match who depends on whom?

skills.title: Why Plants Matter
skills.description: Plants matter to people, animals, and the planet, and we can protect native plants and their homes. Can you pick why plants are important and how to protect them?

skills.title: People's Actions and Plants
skills.description: Building, mowing, and pollution can harm plants, while planting gardens and trees helps. Can you pick actions that hurt or help plants?

skills.title: Locally Grown Food
skills.description: Local food travels a short way and is fresh, but some foods can't grow here all year. Can you pick the good and not-so-good things about local food?

skills.title: Contact and Non-Contact Forces
skills.description: Some forces touch an object, like pushing and friction. Others work from far away, like gravity and magnetism. Can you sort the forces?

skills.title: Ways a Force Is Used
skills.description: A force can push, pull, twist, stretch, squeeze, or hit an object. Can you match each action to the way the force is used?

skills.title: What Forces Do to Objects
skills.description: Forces can start, stop, speed up, slow down, turn, or squish things. A bigger force makes a bigger change. Can you pick what a force does?

skills.title: Forces in Daily Life
skills.description: We use forces when we open doors, kick balls, ride bikes, and brush teeth. Can you pick which force is used in each daily job?

skills.title: Nature's Forces and Our World
skills.description: Wind, water, and gravity can change land and damage buildings, and people can plan to lessen the harm. Can you pick the effects and ways to reduce them?

skills.title: Safety Devices and Forces
skills.description: Forces from things like crashes and falls can hurt people. Helmets, seat belts, and guardrails make the harm smaller. Can you match each device to what it protects?

skills.title: What Is a Structure?
skills.description: A structure is a frame that holds a load and has a size, shape, and job. Can you sort natural and built structures?

skills.title: Form and Function
skills.description: The shape of a structure fits its job, like a wide base for a tower or a curve for a bridge. Can you match each structure's shape to its job?

skills.title: Strength of Structures
skills.description: A strong structure can hold a heavy load. Folding, layering, and shaping materials can make them stronger. Can you pick ways to add strength?

skills.title: Stability of Structures
skills.description: A stable structure keeps its shape, stays balanced, floats, or stays put. A wide, low base helps. Can you pick ways to make a structure more stable?

skills.title: Choosing Building Materials
skills.description: Materials can be strong, flexible, waterproof, or light. Can you pick the best material for a structure?

skills.title: Forces on Structures
skills.description: Wind, weight, and pushes can change a structure's shape, balance, or position. Can you pick what a force does to a structure?

skills.title: Struts and Ties
skills.description: A strut is pushed and squeezed, and a tie is pulled and stretched. Can you tell which part is a strut and which is a tie?

skills.title: Strong Structures Help Us
skills.description: Strong, stable structures keep people safe and affect nature. Can you pick the good and bad effects of structures like bridges and dams?

skills.title: Animal and Human Structures
skills.description: Beavers, birds, and ants build dams, nests, and hills, and people build homes. Can you compare how they affect the environment?

skills.title: What Is in Soil
skills.description: Soil has living parts like worms and roots and non-living parts like sand, clay, and water. Healthy soil is full of life and nutrients. Can you sort the parts?

skills.title: What Gets Added to Soil
skills.description: Fertilizer, compost, pesticides, salt, and spills can go into soil and help or harm it. Can you match each one to its effect?

skills.title: Soil Types and Food
skills.description: Ontario has sandy, clay, loam, and other soils, and each grows different crops best. Can you match each soil to what grows well in it?

skills.title: Erosion
skills.description: Wind, water, and people can carry soil away. This is erosion, and it leaves land poor for plants. Can you pick causes and effects of erosion?

skills.title: Keeping Soil Healthy
skills.description: Farmers and gardeners keep soil healthy by rotating crops, planting cover plants, and adding compost. Can you pick the good soil strategies?

skills.title: Composting
skills.description: Food scraps and leaves rot into compost that feeds soil and cuts waste. Can you put the compost steps in order and pick its benefits?

skills.title: Why Soil Matters
skills.description: Soil grows our food and is a home for many living things. Can you pick why soil is important to people and nature?

skills.title: People's Actions and Soil
skills.description: Farming, building, and pollution can harm soil, but we can protect it. Can you pick actions that hurt or help soil?
